patterns.pattern: Data access is restricted based on user role, with administrators and owners having elevated permissions.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only users with appropriate roles (e.g., admins, document owners) can access or modify sensitive data.

patterns.pattern: Entities (e.g., tickets, invoices, projects, surveys) belong to exactly one parent or are uniquely associated with an owning entity.
patterns.example_phrasing: Each ticket or survey belongs to exactly one customer, project, or workspace.

patterns.pattern: User roles and permissions can be customized at the feature, project, or entity level, affecting what actions users can perform.
patterns.example_phrasing: Permissions can be assigned per user or group for each project or list.

patterns.pattern: Certain actions or information are limited to project members or participants, with non-members denied access.
patterns.example_phrasing: You must be a project member to view or work in the project.

patterns.pattern: Deletion of key entities or user accounts results in cascading deletion or erasure of their associated data.
patterns.example_phrasing: When a user or object is deleted, their related entities (e.g. games, data) are also deleted.

patterns.pattern: Visibility and access can be configured as public, private, or restricted to groups/teams, often at project, document, or view level.
patterns.example_phrasing: Items can be set to public, team, or admins-only visibility.

patterns.pattern: Entities have immutable unique identifiers once created.
patterns.example_phrasing: Each entity gets a unique, non-editable ID at creation.

patterns.pattern: Certain changes or sensitive operations require administrator or owner privileges.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only admins can change permissions or visibility for some items.

patterns.pattern: Audit information or metadata (e.g., roles, obligations, data sensitivity) must be recorded for accountability and compliance.
patterns.example_phrasing: Changes and responsibilities must be logged for compliance.

patterns.pattern: Field assignment, visibility, or participation constraints determined by user or recipient role.
patterns.example_phrasing: Field assignments or participation (e.g., signing) depend on the recipient's role.

patterns.pattern: Lifecycles or state transitions are enforced (e.g., draft before publish; status required for certain actions).
patterns.example_phrasing: Certain actions (like AI detection or publishing) can only be done in specific states (e.g., Draft).

patterns.pattern: User actions and participation are tracked for feature enablement or workflow progression.
patterns.example_phrasing: Participation or completion is tracked (e.g., survey partials, estimate submissions).

patterns.pattern: Data ownership and sensitivity must be tracked for compliance, privacy, or auditing.
patterns.example_phrasing: Ownership and sensitivity of all data must be known and recorded.

patterns.pattern: Quota or response/action limits can be configured, enforcing business constraints or workflow automation (e.g., auto-closing on limit reached).
patterns.example_phrasing: Surveys/campaigns/tickets can be set to auto-close/stop when a configured limit is reached.

patterns.pattern: Public entities (e.g., projects, lists) are accessible to all users within a context unless otherwise restricted.
patterns.example_phrasing: Public projects are viewable by all users in the instance.

patterns.pattern: Data must be stored securely, only when needed, and under the user's control (privacy by design).
patterns.example_phrasing: App listens/stores only when user requests; data is under user control.

patterns.pattern: Compliance requirements (e.g., accessibility, security, retention, logging, device standards) must be documented and met.
patterns.example_phrasing: App must meet accessibility and security standards and document compliance.

patterns.pattern: Default settings (e.g., recipients, visibility) are inherited from team/organization context unless overridden.
patterns.example_phrasing: Defaults are set by team/org but can be overridden at item level.

patterns.pattern: Bulk or batch operations must conform to the same access and integrity constraints as single operations.
patterns.example_phrasing: Bulk actions (like macros) follow usual permission rules.

patterns.pattern: Exporting or sharing data or transcripts is required for user transparency or compliance.
patterns.example_phrasing: Users can export records/transcripts to common formats (e.g. CSV, HTML).
